sections.h2: Where is New London and what is it known for?
sections.html:
New London is a seaport city at the mouth of the Thames River in New London County, on Long Island Sound, and part of the Southeastern Connecticut Planning Region. It is bounded by Waterford on the west and north, the Thames River and Groton on the east, and the Sound on the south.

The city is one of the smallest in Connecticut by land. Of its 10.59 square miles, 5.61 are land and 4.98 are water, so nearly half the area is water. It is home to the U.S. Coast Guard Academy, Connecticut College, Mitchell College and The Williams School. The Norwich to New London metropolitan area includes 21 towns and 274,055 people.

sections.h2: What is New London's history and why does it matter for houses?
sections.html:
New London was first settled by John Winthrop Jr. in 1646 and was officially named New London on March 24, 1658. It was incorporated as a city in 1784. The harbor was considered the best deep water harbor on Long Island Sound, which made it a naval base in the Revolution.

On September 6, 1781, British forces under Benedict Arnold burned much of the city. In the early 19th century it became one of the three busiest whaling ports in the world, alongside Nantucket and New Bedford, and the wealth from whaling funded much of the architecture still standing. Many distinctive 19th-century buildings remain, though the 1853 First Church collapsed in January 2024.

That age shows in the housing. A house built in a port city of this vintage may have old wiring, plumbing and masonry, and buyers who finance with a loan often ask for repairs. A cash sale avoids that step, which suits some owners of older houses.

sections.h2: How do New London property taxes work for a seller?
sections.html:
New London bills real estate tax in two installments, due July 1 and January 1. All bills are mailed in June with enough copies for both installments, and the office does not mail a second bill for real estate or personal property. Second installment bills can be printed from the city's online tax portal.

The grace period for each installment runs through the first day of the next month. For the 2026 to 2027 year, the city lists the January 1, 2027 installment with a last day to pay without penalty of Monday, February 1, 2027. Interest on delinquent taxes accrues at 1.5 percent per month, with a minimum of $2.00 under state statute.

  • Mill rate on the 2025 grand list: 27.10 for real estate, personal property and motor vehicles.
  • City Center District mill rate on the 2025 grand list: 0.99, a separate rate listed for that district.
  • Example from the city: $100,000 of assessed value at 27.10 mills is $2,710 of annual tax.
  • Office: 15 Masonic Street, behind City Hall, open Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.; phone (860) 447-5208.

The tax collector asks owners to update their mailing address with the Assessor when they buy a property, change addresses or pay off a mortgage. If you sell, ask the office for a payoff that includes both installments as of your closing date.

sections.h2: What did the Kelo case mean for Fort Trumbull and New London sellers?
sections.html:
The Fort Trumbull neighborhood is where New London's best-known property case began. The city used eminent domain to take nearly two dozen homes, and the U.S. Supreme Court upheld that in a 5 to 4 ruling in Kelo v. City of New London in 2005.

The homes were demolished as part of an economic development plan, but the chosen developer could not secure financing and the project failed. The empty site has been widely cited as an example of government overreach.

That history is a reminder that any owner can ask the city about planned projects near a property. If your house is near the waterfront or a redevelopment area, call the city's planning office to ask what is proposed, and tell any buyer what you learn.

sections.h2: How does the waterfront climate affect a New London house?
sections.html:
New London has long, hot, humid summers and cool to cold winters. NOAA normals reported on Wikipedia for Groton show an average of 48.91 inches of precipitation a year and 24.5 inches of snow, and the city normally sees snow cover on fewer than 25 days a year.

Hurricanes have struck the Connecticut coast infrequently but with force, with landfalls in 1903, 1938, 1944, 1954 (Carol), 1960 (Donna) and 1985 (Gloria). Tropical Storm Irene in 2011 caused moderate damage along the coast, as did Hurricane Sandy in 2012.

  • Check flood zone status for the lot with your insurer, since a buyer's lender will ask.
  • Look at the roof, siding and windows for wind and salt exposure.
  • Document any past water damage and repairs for the buyer.

sections.h2: How do jobs, ferries and rail connect New London?
sections.html:
New London is a travel hub. Interstate 95 passes through it, and New London Union Station, designed by H.H. Richardson, is served by Amtrak's Northeast Regional and the Shore Line East commuter rail. Bus service includes Southeast Area Transit, Estuary Transit District and Greyhound.

The Cross Sound Ferry to Long Island, the Fishers Island Ferry and the Block Island Ferry all leave from the city, and cruise ships also call. Commercial air service is at T. F. Green Airport and Tweed New Haven. The State Pier is being converted to support offshore wind power.

Defense work is nearby. The Naval Submarine Base New London is physically in Groton, across the river, and the Coast Guard Academy is inside the city. A seller transferring with the military or the Coast Guard may need a closing date that matches orders, and a cash sale can sometimes fit a tight date.

sections.h2: What does the Connecticut conveyance tax cost on a New London sale?
sections.html:
Connecticut taxes a deed when the consideration is $2,000 or more, and the town clerk will not record it until the return is filed and the tax paid.

  • State part on residential property: 0.75 percent up to $800,000, 1.25 percent up to $2,500,000, and 2.25 percent above.
  • Municipal part: 0.25 percent of the price.
  • For a $250,000 sale, the base combined rate of 1 percent is $2,500.
  • A certified pyrrhotite foundation can exempt the first sale of a principal residence.

The statute lets a targeted investment community add up to one-fourth of one percent more. The contract and closing attorney decide who pays.

sections.h2: How can you sell a New London house fast?
sections.html:
Most owners compare listing with an agent against a cash sale. Listing can reach more buyers, but it brings showings, appraisals and repair requests.

  • As-is cash sale: no lender, no repair list, and a closing date set with the title company.
  • Inherited houses: confirm who has authority to sign and whether probate steps are needed.
  • Back taxes: get a payoff from the tax collector so the offer and the closing figures line up.

We review your house and give a written offer with no obligation, and we do not promise a price before we see it. Confirm legal and tax questions with a Connecticut attorney or the city office.

faqs.q: What is the mill rate in New London, CT?
faqs.a: For the 2025 grand list the city lists 27.10 mills for real estate, personal property and motor vehicles, plus 0.99 mills in the City Center District. Confirm the current figure with the tax collector.

faqs.q: When are New London real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: Real estate taxes over $100 are due July 1 and January 1. The city lists the January 1, 2027 installment as last payable without penalty on Monday, February 1, 2027.

faqs.q: Does New London mail the second tax bill?
faqs.a: No. Bills are mailed in June with enough copies for each installment, and the city does not mail second installment bills for real estate. They can be printed from the online tax portal.

faqs.q: How much interest does New London charge on late taxes?
faqs.a: Interest on delinquent taxes accrues at 1.5 percent per month, with a minimum of $2.00 under state statute.

faqs.q: How much is the conveyance tax on a New London house?
faqs.a: For a residential sale up to $800,000 the base combined rate is 1 percent, 0.75 percent state and 0.25 percent municipal. The state rate is higher on the portion above $800,000.

faqs.q: Is New London mostly land or water?
faqs.a: Nearly half the city is water. Of 10.59 square miles total, 5.61 are land and 4.98 are water.
